aiAnalysis.problem_explanation:
### Problem Overview

Insert a new interval into sorted non-overlapping intervals and merge all overlaps.

### Input Specification
N; intervals; final new interval.

### Output Specification
Resulting intervals.

### Constraints
`0≤N≤10^5; endpoints≤10^9.`

### Complexity Target
- Time Complexity: `O(N)`
- Space Complexity: `O(1)` or `O(N)` based on implementation.
aiAnalysis.hint_1: Intervals before the new one are copied untouched, provided they end before its start. For 'Insert and Merge Interval', ensure you understand the required output format.
aiAnalysis.hint_2: Merge every interval overlapping the inserted one, then append the remaining intervals. Consider how the constraints (0≤N≤10^5; endpoints≤10^9.) guide the algorithm choice.
aiAnalysis.hint_3: A single linear pass over the sorted list gives O(N) time and O(N) output space. The target complexity is O(N).
aiAnalysis.brute_force: A straightforward approach directly follows the problem definition: read the input and simulate step-by-step. For Intervals / Arrays problems of this type, a basic repeated scan or O(N²) simulation verifies correctness.
aiAnalysis.optimal_approach: An optimal approach achieves the target complexity of O(N) by applying standard Intervals / Arrays techniques without redundant scanning or allocations.
aiAnalysis.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary space (or O(N) if building an auxiliary result).
